analysis.title: Apple Inc. (AAPL) F4Q26 preview: iPhone 18 family + Duo to drive growth in F2027
key_insights: GS expects in-line F4Q26 results: EPS $2.01 (prior $2.03) vs FactSet consensus $1.99, revenue $113.6bn (+11% yoy) vs consensus $113.4bn, at the high end of company guidance of 9-11% yoy growth.

iPhone revenue is forecast at $56.6bn (+15% yoy), in line with consensus. This reflects a -4% yoy unit decline (in line with IDC) and +20% yoy ASP growth from premium mix and price increases of $100 on the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and on the existing US iPhone lineup.

Services revenue is forecast at about $31.5bn (+10% yoy), in line with consensus and with guidance of F3Q26 growth (+12%) less about 2.5pp of forex headwind. iCloud+, AppleCare+, subscriptions and advertising grow double digits, while App Store grows about +2%.

Gross margin is forecast at 47.8% vs consensus 47.5% and guidance of 47-48% (46-47% excluding tariff refund). It includes about a 1pp benefit from tariff refunds and headwinds from component cost inflation. Partial-quarter pricing benefit in F4Q26 is offset by higher memory costs.

For F1Q27 (December quarter) GS forecasts EPS $2.88 and revenue $151.2bn vs FactSet consensus of $2.92 and $152.2bn, with gross margin 46.8% vs consensus 47.1%. GS expects guidance of low-to-mid single digit yoy revenue growth vs GSe +5%. This is the first full quarter of iPhone price increases.

iPhone 18 Pro series lead times are modestly shorter than the iPhone 17 Pro: 24 days vs 25 days over the first 42 days after orders opened. This may indicate unit demand tracking slightly below the 17 Pro, and may also reflect demand deferral ahead of the iPhone Duo.

iPhone 18 Pro Max lead times held up better, broadly in line with the 17 Pro Max. Reported supply-chain order changes (People's Financial News) are Pro Max +10-15%, Duo +30%, and Pro -10-15%, leaving aggregate Pro-series orders unchanged. GS reads this as a favorable premium mix.

iPhone Duo lead times averaged about 100 days in the first week of pre-orders, consistent across regions. GS cautions that early lead times are inflated by launch hype. Third-party reports say iPhone Duo production yields remain below mature levels and DRAM availability may be delaying A20 Pro device assembly.
Supply constraints are expected to increase significantly sequentially in F4Q26 and affect iPhone, Mac and iPad. Advanced-node SoC availability is the main constraint, per management.

Smartphone market is weak: Counterpoint estimates global shipments fell 20% yoy in 3Q26 and IDC estimates -22%. IDC estimates Apple shipments fell only 4% yoy to 57.3mn, lifting share to 22.4% from 18.2%.

US carrier promotions (AT&T and T-Mobile trade-in credits up to $1,199) and Apple Upgrade (Klarna, 12 or 24 installments) support affordability. Carriers are about 75% of US iPhone unit sales per CIRP.

Mac revenue is forecast at $8.7bn (flat yoy) vs FactSet consensus of +12%. Units fall -12% yoy and ASP rises +13% after average price increases of about 18% in June 2026. GS expects Mac revenue to grow +15% in F2027 on easier comparisons, full-year pricing and M6 launches.
iPad revenue is forecast at $7.4bn (+6% yoy) vs consensus +1%, with units -9% and ASP +17% after average price increases above 20% in June 2026. F2027 iPad revenue is forecast +8%.

iPhone revenue is forecast +7% yoy in F2027, supported by Spring 2027 launches of the base iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2, full-year price increases, the Duo form factor, and carrier promotions.

App Store revenue is forecast at $7.48bn (+2% yoy), decelerating from +3% in F3Q26. Sensor Tower shows C3Q26 App Store spending +2% yoy, with US spending -7% and China +8%. Pressure comes from off-app payment options and commission changes in China, Japan and Brazil, with the China/Japan changes estimated at about a 5pp aggregate headwind.

TAC revenue is forecast at about $7.2bn (+11% yoy), in line with GS's Google TAC growth estimate. Apple TV revenue is forecast at about $2.3bn (+33% yoy) on subscriber growth and August 2026 price increases.
GS expects a Services revenue CAGR of about 9-10% through 2030, reaching $173bn in F30, with App Store at +4% CAGR, iCloud+ +10%, AppleCare+ +11% and Advertising & other +14%.

GS raises its price target to $390 from $360 (40x NTM+1Y EPS vs 37x prior), citing higher confidence in the iPhone replacement cycle after the Duo launch. Rating remains Buy, with 12.2% upside from $347.73.
FY26/27/28 EPS estimates are roughly unchanged: FY26 $8.89 (prior $8.91), FY27 $9.16 (prior $9.14), FY28 $9.76 (prior $9.83). FY26 revenue is $477.96bn (prior $479.43bn).

Key debates are (a) whether hardware demand holds as memory and component costs lift device prices, and whether price/mix can offset unit and margin pressure, and (b) the sustainability of double-digit Services growth given slower App Store trends and regulatory pressure.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $390 from $360 on a 40x NTM+1Y EPS multiple (37x prior), reflecting greater confidence in the iPhone replacement cycle after the iPhone Duo launch. Implies 12.2% upside from $347.73.

sector_views.rationale: GS argues Apple's installed base growth, Services growth and new products should more than offset cyclical product revenue headwinds, with premium positioning a relative advantage as memory inflation pressures lower-end devices.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Memory and component inflation and high device pricing are weighing on end-market demand, while Apple shipments declined only about 4%.
Channels worked through inventory built ahead of price increases. Apple Mac shipments fell 11% yoy per IDC, a smaller decline.

macro_indicators.indicator: Apple App Store spending growth, C3Q26 yoy
macro_indicators.interpretation: Spending slowed from +3% in C2Q26, with the US at -7% and China at +8%.

trade_ideas.description: Buy AAPL, 12-month price target $390 (40x NTM+1Y EPS), 12.2% upside from $347.73
trade_ideas.rationale: Market focus on slower product revenue growth masks ecosystem strength and revenue durability. Services, installed base growth and new products offset cyclical hardware headwinds.
trade_ideas.risk: Weakening consumer demand, supply chain disruption, intensifying competition, regulatory risks, capital allocation execution.

risk_factors: Weakening consumer demand and lengthening iPhone replacement cycles (iPhone was about 50% of FY2025 revenue).
Supply chain disruption: majority of final assembly is in China, with tariff exposure. Supply constraints rise significantly sequentially in F4Q26.
Memory and component cost inflation pressuring margins and device pricing.
Intensifying competition across devices and services, including video streaming.
Regulatory scrutiny, including App Store monetization pressure from off-app payments and commission changes in China, Japan and Brazil.
Capital allocation execution risk in M&A and share repurchases.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows average iPhone 18 Pro lead times of 24 days vs 25 days for the iPhone 17 Pro over the first 42 days, with 18 Pro lead times falling from 22 to 13 days after about 20 days of availability.
Exhibit 24 shows June 2026 Mac price increases averaging 18%, from MacBook Neo $599 to $699 up to M3 Ultra Mac Studio $3,999 to $5,299 (+33%).
Exhibit 29 shows June 2026 iPad price increases averaging 23%, from iPad $349 to $449 (+29%) to 13 inch iPad Pro $1,299 to $1,499 (+15%).
geopolitical: Supply chain risk from final assembly in China and possible tariff disruption from geopolitical tension, as listed in the key risks.
Tariff refund contributes about 1pp to the F4Q26 gross margin guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: Premium positioning, price increases, carrier promotions and Apple Upgrade support iPhone demand, with iPhone revenue +15% in F4Q26E on ASP +20% despite a -4% unit decline. Apple shipments fell far less than the market (-4% vs -22%).
tension_points.bear_case: Higher memory and component costs lift device prices and may cut units. Pro-series lead times are modestly shorter than the 17 Pro, possible Duo demand deferral, supply constraints, and gross margin guided down to 46.8% for F1Q27E from 47.8%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: December-quarter revenue guide below GS's +5% yoy (GS expects LSD-MSD% growth), or unit declines that price/mix cannot offset.

tension_points.bull_case: iCloud+, AppleCare+, subscriptions, advertising and TAC grow double digits, supporting Services of +10% in F4Q26E and about a 9-10% CAGR to 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: App Store growth slows to about +2% on off-app payment options, commission changes in China, Japan and Brazil, and regulatory pressure, with US App Store spending at -7% yoy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: App Store growth turning negative or Services growth falling below the 9.5% yoy guided for F4Q26.
